name: Project Gigabit Kent contract
fact: In May 2026 the Kent CityFibre contract was redesigned from around 50,000 to around 9,000 premises as commercial rollout changed.
gate: Earlier contract quantities are superseded and must not be used as current address-level coverage.

name: Project Gigabit East and West Sussex contract
fact: In May 2026 the East and West Sussex contract was revised to around 13,000 premises because commercial rollout and market conditions changed.
gate: Contract redesign proves programme scope can move; exact address status must be rechecked.

name: Project Gigabit Buckinghamshire Hertfordshire East Berkshire contract
fact: The May 2026 redesign reduced this CityFibre Project Gigabit contract to around 6,000 premises.
gate: Do not promote based on the original contract footprint; current scope and service availability are separate states.

name: Project Gigabit Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire contract
fact: BDUK states CityFibre is no longer delivering this Project Gigabit contract after mutual termination in 2026.
gate: A historic contract must be rejected as current build evidence unless a replacement programme/address check confirms service.

name: Project Gigabit North Shropshire contract
fact: After Freedom Fibre could not complete the original contract, BDUK added North Shropshire premises to Openreach call-off three in April 2026.
gate: Supplier and contract identity can change; only the latest programme state may be used.

name: Project Gigabit Derbyshire Peak District contract
fact: BDUK and FullFibre terminated the Peak District contract and in April 2026 moved the area into an Openreach Project Gigabit contract change.
gate: Terminated supplier scope is historical; replacement contract still does not prove an address is live.

name: Project Gigabit Cheshire contract
fact: Freedom Fibre's Cheshire contract was terminated and a February 2026 Openreach call-off eight was added for about 18,500 hard-to-reach premises.
gate: Previous supplier scope is not current evidence; replacement contract award is not an orderable-service state.

name: Project Gigabit Cornwall contracts
fact: In February 2026 BDUK reported Wildanet would not fully complete two Cornwall contracts, after about 13,200 premises had been covered and about 7,700 remained.
gate: Programme delivery can stop or be replanned; historic contracted premises are not guaranteed future serviceability.

name: Project Gigabit West Herefordshire and Forest of Dean contract
fact: BDUK terminated the FullFibre contract and in April 2026 included West Herefordshire within Openreach call-off three.
gate: Replacement planning is not evidence that every previous premises is built or orderable.

name: Project Gigabit Bedfordshire Northamptonshire Milton Keynes contract
fact: In May 2026 the contract was redesigned to around 6,000 premises, down from the original around 25,000, because commercial rollout changed.
gate: Original contract quantity cannot be treated as current coverage or development-site serviceability.

name: Openreach where and when Full Fibre build map
fact: Openreach says its map shows exchange-level build progress while its postcode checker gives the more personalised property view; plans and dates can change.
gate: Exchange-level colour/build plan is not proof that a particular parcel or address can order Full Fibre.

name: Openreach help for property developers
fact: Openreach provides developer guidance for connecting new residential and mixed-use sites to Full Fibre.
gate: Developer support availability is not a site agreement, completed network build or retail service order.

name: Openreach Fibre broadband availability checker
fact: Openreach distinguishes 'available to order now', 'available soon', 'planning to build', 'building now' and 'no plans yet' states, and says build plans can change.
gate: Only 'available to order now' is an orderable state; planning/building/soon must not be promoted as live service.

name: Openreach broadband network overview
fact: Openreach links its fibre checker, build plans and community partnership routes from its broadband-network overview.
gate: Network technology availability at operator level does not establish serviceability at a target development.

name: Openreach Full Fibre broadband for developers
fact: Openreach offers Full Fibre infrastructure for new residential, mixed-use and commercial developments and says project-specific estimates follow site registration/survey.
gate: Eligibility, free-build thresholds or product options are not proof a specific site has a completed or accepted network design.

name: Openreach developer contracts and policies
fact: Openreach requires developers to communicate site changes and documents Full Fibre-focused new-site policy as the copper network is retired.
gate: Policy direction does not replace the signed site agreement, wayleave or current project design.

name: Openreach registering your site
fact: Openreach says a registration leads to a new-sites agreement/wayleave and the application cannot proceed without return of the agreement unless a framework agreement exists.
gate: Site registration is not network acceptance or live broadband; signed contractual and build stages remain required.

name: Openreach developer resources
fact: Openreach provides step-by-step developer-portal resources for preparing new sites for fibre connections.
gate: Portal/resources usage is process evidence only and does not establish completed infrastructure.

name: Openreach main network portal
fact: Openreach identifies its developer portal as the route for housebuilders, developers and architects to manage new residential or commercial network builds.
gate: Operator-portal availability is not a site-specific network state.

name: Openreach Fibre Community Partnership
fact: Fibre Community Partnerships are an alternative for communities outside build plans and can depend on survey, funding, validated voucher pledges and later service orders.
gate: Expression of interest, voucher eligibility or pledged funding is not a completed network or live service.

name: Openreach Full Fibre programmes explained
fact: Openreach explains commercial, new-sites, multi-dwelling, government and community programmes can have different geographic scales and delivery timescales.
gate: Programme membership or exchange-area planning must not replace the address-level checker and exact development agreement.
